935 PM EST Mon Nov 16 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Have added mention of freezing fog to the forecast tonight,
particularly across mountain and river valleys.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Dry conditions persist through the end of the week as 
  temperatures gradually increase.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry conditions persist through the end of the week 
as temperatures gradually increase.

For tonight, stout high pressure combined with light winds and
mainly clear skies will support ample raditional cooling
effects. With dew points currently in the low/mid 30s and
expected to lower a bit overnight, temperatures will sit near
freezing as the ground cools. Patchy fog may develop across the
mountain and river valleys, some of it which may turn into
freezing fog given temperatures in the upper 20s to low 30s.
Have a Special Weather Statement out for this threat, especially
along and west of I-81.

Broad high pressure will build over the central Plains in the 
upper levels, while transitioning to a surface high pressure 
over the mid-Atlantic. This ridge will influence dry conditions 
and gradually increasing temperatures through the rest of the 
week. Plenty of sunshine each day with highs approaching the 
middle to upper 60s to near 70 by Friday across the region. Lows
at night will remain in the 30s to 40s through the week. One 
caveat to the prolonged dry conditions and warming temperatures 
could have implications on fire weather (see Fire Weather 
section below). 

Looking towards next weekend, it is still looking quite dry at
this point, but there are some hints at some activity in both
branches of the jet stream going into early next week. At this
juncture, not seeing any significant precipitation potential.
The two indications of possible precipitation chances will be a
trough of low pressure extending northwestward from a coastal
low near the Carolina Coast and an approaching cold front from
the Ohio Valley. As of now, there are only slight chances to
chances of rain showers Saturday night into Sunday.

&&

.AVIATION /02Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Mainly dry for all TAF sites through the upcoming week.
VFR conditions are anticipated through the end of the week as 
high pressure remains in control. Skies should remain mostly 
clear, with winds staying below 10 knots generally. Winds 
generally flow WSW before shifting northwesterly Friday.

&&

.MARINE...
Northwest winds will continue to diminish and should become
light and variable or calm at times through much of the week.
Winds are expected to shift southerly by Thursday night before
shifting back to the north on Friday, generally staying below 10
knots.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
High pressure gradually builds overhead into the middle of the 
week, then temperatures will begin to warm mid to late week. 
During this timeframe, while winds will diminish, RH values 
will go down substantially. The dry air really builds in 
starting Tuesday into Tuesday night, and looks to continue for 
several days thereafter. Overnight recoveries, especially on the
ridges, will likely be very poor as well starting Tuesday 
night. Expect afternoon RH values to drop well into the 20s each
day. This will also be paired with seasonably warm temperatures,
so this will really act to dry out already very dry fuels.

Not helping matters is that there is no precipitation expected 
east of the Appalachians likely through at least the first half
of next weekend. Given the setup, will really be watching for 
any potential dry frontal passages in the long range as the next
days to really watch out for. There is a non-zero chance that 
some rain could come into the forecast early next week, but 
there is very little model agreement at this point, and it seems
just as likely that we could see another dry frontal passage in
this timeframe. So, just continue to monitor the latest 
forecast over the next several days as models hopefully come 
into better agreement.
